note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM F, team 1916704: a four-model argument about a central-bank-issued global digital
currency. Model 1 is a DSGE feasibility test; section 4 screens fourteen indicators by PCA;
Model 2 classifies money-laundering sectors by kNN on a vector-space embedding; Model 3 forecasts
the spillover with a spatial autoregressive model on 163 countries. Twenty-one pages, ten of which
carry art, thirteen measured regions.

**All thirteen are accounted**: 6 figure rows and 7 grids, and **nothing refused** - the first
paper in this stretch where every measured region is an exhibit. The eighth printed table,
**Table 2 "Parameter Calibration Table of Model 1" on p8, prints a full grid and owns no measured
region at all**; it is declared in the deficits list and in this note rather than given an
invented bbox.

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 1.2 "Our work" takes **Figure 1**, the roadmap, after the fourth numbered task and before the
  heading of section 2. Nothing introduces it.
- 3.2 "Variable Nomenclature" takes **Table 1** - but the grid prints ABOVE the heading, so the
  page opens with the glossary and the section it belongs to is announced underneath it.
- 3.4 "Implementation and Results" takes **Tables 2 and 3**. Table 2 is the calibration
  (unmeasured), Table 3 the steady-state answer. The reader meets them in the order
  calibration-then-result, which is what makes the missing box a loss rather than a nuisance.
- 3.5 "Future Discussion" takes **Figure 2**, the impulse responses; it is the only figure whose
  panels sit in the section whose conclusion they support rather than in the implementation one.
- 4 "Key Factors: PCA" takes **Tables 4 and 5** back to back at the top of one page, and no
  heading intervenes: the variance decomposition and the loading matrix are one exhibit split
  into two grids.
- 5.2.3 and 5.2.5 take **Table 6** (glossary) and then **Figures 3 and 4** (the scatter and the
  classified scatter), one per page.
- 6.2 takes **Table 7** (glossary); 6.4 takes **Table 8** (coefficients) and **Figure 5** (the
  ten-per-cent test); 6.5 takes **Figure 6** (the five-per-cent test).

The pattern is a **house style**: every model opens with a glossary grid (Table 1, Table 6,
Table 7) and closes with one results object. The three glossaries are the same construction,
cut down each time - 31 rows, then 13, then 7 - as the models get smaller.

## When it goes 3-D

**Never.** Six figures, no perspective projection, no surface, no isometric drawing, no colourbar
anywhere. The DSGE output is two flat panels, the kNN output is a scatter in a plane, the SAR
output is six flat time series. The paper's own third dimension - the fourteen PCA dimensions -
is collapsed to two by the projection and then never plotted as depth.

## What the figures do

| group | count | what it actually is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Figure 1 | 1 | five-box vertical flowchart with bracketed leaves |
| Figure 2 | 1 (2 panels) | DSGE impulse responses, consumption and output, 25 periods |
| Figure 3 | 1 | eleven labelled training points in a bare rectangle, no axes |
| Figure 4 | 1 | the same eleven points, a red boundary, one hand-drawn circle |
| Figure 5 | 1 (3 panels) | SAR indicator levels under a 10% shock |
| Figure 6 | 1 (3 panels) | the same three indicators under a 5% shock |

**The paper has two plotting modes and no third.** Everything a machine produced is a raster
MATLAB export (Figures 2, 5, 6) with numbered ordinates, no x axis, and a legend chip that
repeats the panel title. Everything a hand produced is vector (Figure 1) or a bare scatter with
no axes at all (Figures 3 and 4). There is no bar, no histogram, no box plot, no heatmap, no map
in the whole file.

**Figures 3 and 4 are the same data twice** - the second adds a boundary and a circle, never a
new point. And **Figures 5 and 6 are the same three panels twice**, differing only in the growth
assumption and therefore in the ordinate scale, which is why the paper prints both instead of
tabulating the sensitivity.

## Table shapes worth reusing

| table | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table 1 | 31x4 | the standard glossary: 'Abbreviation / Description' printed twice across the head |
| Table 2 | 14x2 | the calibration: parameter/value pairs, no rule under the last row measured |
| Table 3 | 3x3 | the result: level down the stub, two named ratios across the head |
| Table 4 | 3x5 | the PCA screen-plot transposed - metrics as rows, components as columns |
| Table 5 | 14x5 | the loading matrix, six decimals, signs are the finding |
| Table 6 | 13x4 | Table 1's construction, cut to half the rows, one row unpaired |
| Table 7 | 7x4 | Table 1's construction again, cut to seven rows |
| Table 8 | 2x7 | coefficients only: a stub cell and six vectors, two body rows |

Every one is **booktabs** - a rule above the header, a rule under it, a closing rule - with no
vertical rule, no shading, no merged cell and no diagonal anywhere in the file. That is the
opposite of #187, whose numbered grids were boxed colour blocks: this paper's grids are LaTeX
tables, and the difference tracks whether the model was typeset or pasted.

**Two grids transpose the usual orientation to save height**: Table 4 puts metrics in rows and
components in columns so a 3x5 grid says what a 5x3 would; Table 8 puts six estimated vectors in
the header and only the two parameter families in the stub.

## Caption template

**One dialect, no seam.** All thirteen captions are `Number: phrase`, colon attached, one space
after it:

- `Figure 1: Our Work`
- `Figure 2: The impact of the technical shock of central bank digital currency on consumption and output`
- `Figure 3: Data visualization` (printed truncated; the phrase continues as body prose)
- `Table 8: Model estimation coefﬁcient` (the file's one singular-for-plural fault)

Captions print BELOW all six figures and ABOVE all seven grids. **Not one caption ends in a full
stop**: Figure 3's runs `Figure 3: Data visualization` and the sentence-stop belongs to the body
paragraph that swallowed the rest of the phrase, and Figure 4's is the bare noun phrase
`Classiﬁcation result graph`. Every MATLAB export's caption is likewise a bare noun phrase.
**The caption never states the parameter that distinguishes the figure from its twin** - Figures
5 and 6 are a 10% and a 5% shock, and neither caption says so; the number lives only in the prose
that points at each one. Table 7's caption is correctly above its grid, but the text layer prints
the grid's first head cell ahead of it.

## Context connectives

- **Eight of the thirteen exhibits are named by number in prose**, and four of those pointers are
  the sentence's opening clause: `Figure 2 shows that`, `Figure 4 gave an example of k = 3.`,
  `As can be seen from the Figure 5`, `Figure 6 is the result of a test with a growth of 5%.`
- **Two of the pointers are parenthetical or trailing**: `observed data distribu- tion(Figure 3)`
  and `we only consider the indirect effect here) and sort it into Table 8`, where the pointer is
  the tail of a sentence about the arithmetic, not about the grid.
- **`Table 3` is the only exhibit cited twice**, once before it (`See Table 3 for details.`) and
  once after it (`It can also be seen from Table 3 that when ℓ = 1...`), which is the clearest
  pointer-and-read-back pair in the paper.
- **Five exhibits get no pointer at all**: Figure 1, Table 1, Table 4, Table 6 and Table 7 - and
  four of those five are the glossaries and the roadmap, i.e. the exhibits the reader is expected
  to find by looking rather than by being sent.
- Only three exhibits get a read-back sentence, and all three read the RESULT rather than the
  drawing: Figure 2's, Figure 4's and Table 3's.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **Table 2 prints and is never boxed.** The p8 layout pass returns one region, at y 481.5-534.8,
  which is Table 3's body rows; the calibration grid at the top of the same page returns nothing.
  A caption-to-object matcher therefore pairs Table 2's caption with Table 3's box.
- **Table 3's measured box is its grid and only its grid** (y 481.5-534.8, three rules apart):
  the caption at y 471.6 sits outside it, so a box-to-caption proximity rule sees a 9.9 pt gap
  and a grid whose top edge is a rule, not a title.
- **Table 7's caption is above the grid, but the text layer prints it second.** Extraction gives
  the first line as `Abbreviation            Table 7: Variable Nomenclature of Model 3` - the
  first header cell and the caption share one baseline row - so a text-layer reader meets a
  stray head cell before the title even though the printed page obeys the class rule.
- **Figure 3's caption is truncated on the page.** The typeset line is `Figure 3: Data
  visualization`; the phrase continues as the opening of the next body paragraph (`into
  two-dimensional vectors. Then we projected them...`), so the title has to be welded from two
  blocks and a caption regex reads the figure as 'Data visualization'.
- **Two Table 5 stub cells are lost.** The 'Exchange rate' and 'Unemployment rate' labels print
  detached at the foot of the block, after the numbers they label, so the text layer reads two
  rows as bare number runs.
- **The printed page number is offset by two**: PDF page 3 prints `Page 1 of 19`, PDF page 18
  prints `Page 16 of 19`, and PDF page 21 prints `Page 19 of 19`, so the count of 19 excludes the
  sheet and the contents page and the offset stays constant to the end. The running head is
  `Team # 1916704` at the left with the page number at the right, above a rule, on every page.
- **The table of contents parses as headings**: p2 contributes eight entries of the form
  `3 Model 1: Financial System Construction−DSGE Model 2`, where the trailing digit is the
  printed page number welded onto the title, so the heading index lists each model on p2.
- **One heading is a formula fragment**: p6 indexes `2 Pt−1(z)` as a numbered heading, an
  equation's exponent swept into the heading detector.
- **Sentences glue at exhibit boundaries**: `k = 3.The red line`, `here) and sort it into
  Table 8`, `abovea˛łthe sum total`, `currency(In 2015`. The paragraph break disappears while the
  punctuation survives.

## Declared deficits

**One: Table 2.** The paper prints `Table 2: Parameter Calibration Table of Model 1` on p8 at
y 258.6 over a four-column calibration grid - one head line `Parameter Calibration Value` under a
rule at y 268.4, nine data rows carrying two parameter/value pairs each, and a closing rule at
y 386.3 - i.e. eighteen parameters: β 0.7, ρv 0.8, ϕ 1, ρw 0.6, α 0.5, ρ 0.8, γ 0.7, ρr1 0.8,
χ 0.02%, ρr2 0.8, δ 2%, ϕP 4, w 0.2, ϕk 4, σ 0.60%, r10 0.40%, µ 5, r20 2%. The layout pass
returned no region over y 258.6-386.3 at all; its one p8 region is Table 3's grid at
y 481.5-534.8, 95 points lower and belonging to the next table. No bbox exists, so no row is
recorded; the grid is named here and in the payload's deficit list instead.
rules: Every grid in the file is the same construction - a rule above the header, a rule under it, a closing rule, no vertical rule, no shading, no merged cell, no diagonal - across seven numbered tables from p5 to p17. Boxed grids belong to pasted images; typeset grids are booktabs, and this paper typesets all seven. [table.rule_style]

A model's glossary is a fixed opening exhibit: each of the three models gets one at its variable-nomenclature section, and the three shrink with the models - 31 rows, then 13, then 7 - while keeping 'Abbreviation / Description' printed twice across the head. [table.cols]

A grid that would be too tall is transposed rather than split: Table 4 puts three metrics in rows and four components in columns, and Table 8 puts six estimated vectors in the header with only the two parameter families in the stub. [table.rows]

The unit is written into the header cell, never into the body: Table 3's 'Deposit reserve ratio(m/d)' and 'Household consumption as a share of GDP(c/y)' carry the ratio in the header while every body value prints as a bare percentage. [table.units_in_header]
No grid carries a note line, a source line or a units row anywhere in the file; everything note-like about a table is printed as running prose before or after it. [table.note_sentence]

Numeric columns are centred, not decimal-aligned: Table 8's cells are centred in their columns so the decimal points shift whenever a value changes width, and Table 5 prints six signed decimals of a loading matrix whose signs, not whose places, are the finding. [table.decimal_aligned]

Captions print BELOW every figure and ABOVE every grid without exception - but the text layer does not preserve that order: Table 7's first head cell and its caption share one baseline row, so extraction emits 'Abbreviation  Table 7: ...' as a single line and a text-layer reader meets the grid before its title. [caption.position]

The dialect is a single 'Number: phrase' with the colon attached, from p3 to p18, with no seam and no spelling variant, and **not one caption in the file ends in a full stop** - the only sentence-stopped-looking one, Figure 3, is a caption the typesetter cut in half, its remainder typeset as the next paragraph. [caption.numbering]

A caption never states the parameter that distinguishes an exhibit from its twin: Figures 5 and 6 are a 10% and a 5% shock and neither caption says which, so the number is only in the prose that points at it. [caption.conditions]

Numbering follows the press here, not the argument - Figures 1 to 6 and Tables 1 to 8 all print in numeric order - which is the inverse of #187, where Figure 5 printed after 6 and 7. [place.doc_order]

A model's section can open with the exhibit printed before its heading: Table 1 fills the top of p5 and the heading '3.2 Variable Nomenclature' prints underneath it, so a heading-first chunker assigns the grid to the section above. [place.section_path]
Eight of thirteen exhibits are named by number in prose, and half of those pointers open the sentence ('Figure 2 shows that', 'Figure 4 gave an example of k = 3.'). [mention.count]

The pointer can be parenthetical or trailing rather than a lead-in clause: '(Figure 3)' sits inside the sentence that hands the reader the projection, and 'sort it into Table 8' is the tail of a sentence about the arithmetic, not about the grid. [mention.lead_pattern]

The exhibits nobody points at are the ones the reader is meant to find by looking: the roadmap and all three glossaries are uncited, while every results grid and every plotted figure but Figure 1 is named. [mention.first_page]

Read-back sentences read the result, never the drawing: the three that exist explain what the shock does to consumption and output, what class the nearest three points belong to, and which ℓ the steady state favours - no sentence describes an axis, a curve or a marker. [mention.trail_sentence]
3-D is never a solution: a fourteen-dimensional PCA is projected to two by the method and plotted flat, and the SAR's third dimension is time, printed as six separate traces. [geometry.three_d]

Machine output is raster and hand output is not: every MATLAB export (Figures 2, 5 and 6) is a numbered-ordinate raster with no x axis, while the scatter, the classified scatter and the roadmap are vector art with no numbers at all. [geometry.family]

Where a figure has panels, the panels are repeated titles rather than letters: Figures 5 and 6 print 'banking', 'economy', 'trading' in bold above each frame and then repeat the same word in a legend chip inside it. [geometry.panel_layout]

Every raster legend repeats its panel title, so no legend in the file carries information the title did not: 'banking' beside a blue line under the bold title 'banking'. The two scatters are the only figures whose legend says something new ('High', 'Medium', 'Low'). [geometry.legend]
Panels are never shared-axis: the three SAR frames sit at one height with three different ordinate scales (0-0.10, 0-0.07, 0-0.25), so their traces look comparable and are not. [geometry.shared_axes]
